title: Renewal Velocity & Technical Expansion Brief — Dedicated/Private/SLA Pathways
content:
Purpose and scope:
This is a working brief and lightweight QBR + renewal tracker template focused on converting mid-to-large customers from hosted usage to Dedicated Capacity and/or Private deployments, and/or adding premium SLA bundles. The doc is intentionally tactical — blending customer economics, technical gating, and phased play sequencing that CS reps can adapt for each account.

Intended audience:
- CS Managers and Account Owners (AEs looped for commercial terms)
- Solutions Engineering for technical validation and scoping
- Sales leadership for approval on pricing/discounting bands

Status: draft — living doc for 1:1 tailoring. Open questions tagged with [QUESTION].

1) One-page executive QBR template (to hand to executive sponsors)
- Objective: summarize health, spend trend, risk, and a single recommended next step (Dedicated / Private / SLA). Keep to one page.
- Top-line bullets: current ARR or monthly spend, 90-day token trend (+/- %), latency or error incidents this quarter, key product adoption signals (chat sessions/day, embedding QPS), recommended action and business impact (delta ARR, cost predictability, SLA uplift).
- Example (fill-in):
  Customer: Acme Retail
  Current spend: $28k/mo hosted API (avg)
  90-day spend growth: +18%
  SRE incidents (P1): 1 (2026-01-12)
  Adoption signals: 2 teams using embeddings + 1 customer-facing chat flow
  Recommended next step: Pilot Dedicated 4-GPU pool (3 month trial) to lock-in 30% per-token cost reduction and guaranteed latency SLA (p50<120ms).

2) Renewal Velocity Tracker (compact CSV-like template for paste into sheets)
- Columns: account, renewal_date, current_contract_value, forecasted_conversion, recommended_offer, primary_owner, SE_assigned, technical_risk, exec_sponsor, next_action_date, status
- Sample rows:
  Acme Retail,2026-08-15,$336000,75%,Dedicated-4GPU-trial,Aisha M,D.Park,medium,CTO (J. Lee),2026-03-28,proposal-sent
  FinHealth Inc,2026-05-01,$120000,40%,Private-VPC-PoC,Maya S,O.Haddad,high,CISO (R. Chen),2026-03-20,technical-eval

3) Commercial offer bands & negotiation play (quick reference)
- Standard: 10–50k/mo hosted -> suggest Dedicated starter; small discount (5–10%) for 12mo commit
- Mid: 50–250k/mo -> propose Dedicated with reserved capacity + 10–20% discount, include 1-onboarding SE day and 30-day operational support SLA
- Enterprise: 250k+ -> Private deployment with custom SLA, negotiated network/KMS integration costs; price band is case-by-case (protect margin)
- SLA add-ons: bronze (uptime 99.5, target response 24h), silver (99.9, 8h), gold (99.95, 1h + runbook reviews). Typical uplift: bronze +6–8% MRR, silver +12–15%, gold +18–25% (subject to capacity/ops cost).
- [QUESTION] We should formalize discount guardrails per ARR band — track with Finance.

4) Technical gating checklist (SE checklist for Dedicated -> Private readiness)
- Workload and footprint: baseline token/day, peak TPS, typical sequence length distribution
- Data residency/ingress: confirm VPC requirements, egress limits, allowed IP ranges, KMS/HSM needs
- Model compatibility: list models in use, quantization tolerance, custom finetunes or prompt-layer logic
- Integration shape: API vs SDK vs on-prem adapter; function calling usage; streaming needs
- Observability needs: required retention for logs/tracing, PII redaction, audit frequency
- Runbook/DR: desired RTO/RPO, fallback model plan, canary rollout cadence
- Security review status: SSO/OAuth, SCIM, SOC2 evidence, penetration test window
- [SE action] produce a 2-week technical feasibility note and rough cost estimate.

5) Play sequencing & ownership (step-by-step)
- Phase 0 (Discovery): CS owner runs economics workshop (30–45 min) with the customer; gather workload metrics and business sponsors. Deliverable: one-pager with estimated spend delta and recommended path. (Owner: CS lead)
- Phase 1 (Proof of Value - PoV): spin up Dedicated pilot (4–12 weeks) or Private PoC (shorter timeline but heavier onboarding). Deliverables: pilot KPIs dashboard, performance baseline, SE findings doc. (Owner: CS + SE)
- Phase 2 (Commercial/Procurement): AE involved; negotiate term and SLAs; finance ops finalize applied discounts. (Owner: AE + CS)
- Phase 3 (Onboarding & Rollout): SRE/Infra/Customer IT validate; migration plan executed; 30/60/90 day success check-ins. (Owner: Solutions Eng + CS)

6) Risk matrix (simple):
- Technical risk: high/medium/low (based on model compat, infra readiness)
- Commercial risk: churn likelihood if no action taken (High if >30% ARR at risk)
- Timing risk: procurement window, external dependencies (legal, network).
- Mitigation examples: phased trial, conditional discounts tied to usage, rollback to hosted fallback model during cutover.

7) QBR talking points (usable script fragments for CS reps)
- For exec sponsor: "In the last 90 days, your platform generated X embeddings and Y generated responses. Moving to Dedicated gives predictable unit economics and a performance SLA which matters as you push customer-facing features into production. We recommend a 90-day Dedicated pilot to validate latency and cost improvements."
- For technical sponsor: "We’ll run a short PoV to capture tail-latency, peak TPS, and KV cache hit rates. Our SE will validate model build and any quantization tolerances; most customers see cost reduction from batching/caching within 2–3 weeks."

8) Sample email templates (short and editable)
- Exec ask (one-liner):
  Subject: Quick QBR follow-up + recommended pilot
  Hi <ExecName>,
  Quick follow-up from our QBR — we recommend a short Dedicated pilot that should lower your per-token costs ~25% and cap latency spikes observed last quarter. Can we align on a 90-day pilot with a check-in at 30/60 days?
  Thanks,
  <CS Owner>

- Technical kickoff:
  Subject: PoV kickoff — tech scope and next steps
  Hi <EngineerName>,
  Attaching the SE scope doc and the data collection checklist. We need sample traffic for 72 hours and an SSO test user. Proposed kickoff: <date>.
  Thanks,
  <SE Name>

9) KPIs to measure success (proposal for dashboards)
- Commercial: ARR expansion delta, NRR contribution, conversion rate from trial to committed
- Performance: p50/p95 latency, tail-latency events, token cost per 1M tokens
- Reliability: number of P1/P2 incidents, mean time to investigate (MTTI), SLA compliance %
- Adoption: feature-enabled sessions, daily active users per integration

10) Internal playbook checklist (for CS Manager review before submitting offer)
- [ ] Confirm exec sponsor alignment
- [ ] SE feasibility note attached
- [ ] Pricing band approved by revenue ops
- [ ] Draft SLA attached (if applicable)
- [ ] Rollback/fallback plan documented
- [ ] Proposed success metrics with 30/60/90 day check-ins

11) Appendix: quick heuristics and notes
- Heuristic: customers with predictable, high-volume batch workloads (large embedding pipelines, nightly indexing) see the fastest ROI on Dedicated capacity. Real-time customer-facing chat with spiky TPS is a good candidate for Private + gold SLA.
- Note on cost modeling: include both per-token CPU/GPU costs and ops overhead for private deployments (networking, KMS, on-call).
- Unresolved: clarify how committed burst capacity is priced for Dedicated (Engineering pricing policy doc link needed). [ACTION: Finance/Eng pricing sync — JIRA CS-7891].

12) Next actions for this document (meta):
- Iterate with Revenue Ops to lock discount guardrails (owner: Aisha)
- Create a canonical Google Sheet from the Renewal Velocity CSV above and link it in the Confluence QBR Methods page (owner: Daniel)
- Run a templated outreach experiment for 20 mid ARR accounts this quarter and report conversion (owner: Maya)

----
Notes to self (informal):
- Keep this one-pager lean — executive buy-in is sensitive to clarity not exhaustive tables.
- Add a one-click checklist card in the CS console with prefilled metrics for quick email generation.
- Capture 2 anonymized case studies from customers who migrated in the last 6 months to include in QBR decks.

End of draft.
